Bounds on a sentence's effect without assumptions

Source: R/corr.R
sntbnd.Rd

Each person receives one of two sentences and shows the outcome (say, reconviction) under that one only. With no assumption about who receives which, the chance of the outcome under a sentence is known only up to an interval whose width is the share who received the other sentence, and the effect of one sentence against the other lies in an interval of width exactly 1 that always contains 0: observational data alone cannot even sign it. See proof("sntbnd").

Usage

sntbnd(y, z, treat = NULL, w = NULL)

Arguments

y

Outcomes: 0 or 1 for each person.

z

Sentences: a vector with exactly two distinct values, same length: character, numbers, logical or a factor (its labels; level order and whether it is ordered are ignored), not dates.

treat

The value of z taken as the treatment, matched exactly; NULL for the second in sorted order. The values are sorted as text by Unicode code point ("B" before "a", "10" before "2"), the same on every machine whatever its locale.

w

NULL for equal weights, or one non-negative weight per person with a positive total.

Value

A data frame with three rows, the comparison sentence, the treatment and effect (treatment minus comparison): term, share (the weighted share sentenced; NA for the effect), lower, upper and observed (the observed rate under each sentence and their difference).

References

Manski, C. F. and Nagin, D. S. (1998). Bounding disagreements about treatment effects: a case study of sentencing and recidivism. Sociological Methodology, 28(1), 99-137. doi:10.1111/0081-1750.00043

Examples

set.seed(1)
z <- sample(c("community", "custody"), 500, TRUE, c(0.6, 0.4))
y <- rbinom(500, 1, ifelse(z == "custody", 0.55, 0.35))
sntbnd(y, z)
#>        term share  lower upper  observed
#> 1 community 0.624  0.208 0.584 0.3333333
#> 2   custody 0.376  0.192 0.816 0.5106383
#> 3    effect    NA -0.392 0.608 0.1773050
